Judge: The better image is clearly better in all four pairs: pair 1 A, pair 2 A, pair 3 B and pair 4 B. None is close to indistinguishable. The four weaker frames all show the same Marina-Bay-style landmark set (three towers with a sky-deck, a lotus museum, supertrees, a helix bridge), and they share the same faults. Lighting is flat, with no clear sun direction and missing cast shadows, so towers, trees, lamps and people look like they float. There is no haze gradient through depth. Towers are box extrusions with tiling striped facades. Vegetation is sparse and low-poly. Spaces are empty, with almost no people, props or signage. Clouds are cartoon sprites, and the bridge has a black void at its vanishing point. Two good signs: pair 3's warm low sun with raking helix shadows shows the renderer can produce mood, and pair 2's over-the-shoulder framing is sound. The winning frames get their believability from dense, specific set dressing, consistent sunlight, strong atmospheric perspective and cinematic framing, although their texture detail is dated by modern standards. Only the air-to-air helicopter shot (pair 1 A) and the golden-haze view past the hillside sign (pair 4 B) genuinely wow. Two of the winning frames (pair 1 A and pair 3 B) carry a commercial game logo in the image itself. I judged on visual merit only, and the verdicts would not change without the logos. The highest-leverage fixes for the weaker set, in order: sun direction and cast shadows; a haze gradient through depth; crowds and street-level props; facade materials that don't visibly repeat.
